title: Japanese Money Methods
note:
THE NUMBER THAT TRAVELLED. -hi parity pass (editor en-ch2-3). The four
     chapter-2 Lotties are spent here exactly as -hi spends them — the table row
     pulled out of its source (s15), the two rates drawn to scale (s17), the
     households counted and not counted (s19), the number that travels (s20).
     Four is the cap, so no fifth is available and none is wanted.

     s16 is a TRUTH fix: the nub is 16px in a 1480px track = 1.08%, under a focal
     reading ABOUT 1%. The previous build drew the same 16px nub in a 600px
     track — 2.67% — which overstated a published figure by 2.4x on screen.
     Anything that reads as a published figure must BE one.

     s13/s15/s16/s17 carry their art in a FULL-FRAME p-a window, not in B's
     860x610 p-b plate. The plate's edge rule read as a UI panel pasted on the
     photograph, and slice-cropping a 1920-wide drawing into it is what turned
     s17's two bars into two smudges hard right. The art now sits in the picture,
     which is what -hi does.

     Ground arc: warm promise -> cool screen-light -> amber under examination ->
     neutral -> amber deeper -> THE COLDEST FRAME IN THE CUT where the claim
     collapses to about one per cent -> red at the correction -> neutral -> cool
     -> red radiating -> warm resolve. The drop is a temperature event before it
     is a number.

     Archetypes: A A B A B B B A D D A — B held across s15/s16/s17 because
     37.8% -> about 1% -> thirty times is one argument, and D across s19/s20
     because both of those scenes are a mechanism in the lower two-thirds.

     s21 is US-market and is NOT -hi: four twenty-dollar bills, $4,000, Census
     P60-286. Never copy -hi's s21 here.

s11.comment:
2.1 · A · PLATE · fund · warm — THREE METHODS. A lit shopfront: a threshold
     you are about to walk through, which is what 'three methods' opens.

s12.comment:
2.2 · A · PLATE · no role · cool — THE FEED. A hand scrolling a lit phone;
     this is screen light and the ground says so.

s13.comment:
2.3 · B · FIGURE · target · amber — THE INTERNET SAYS. The line is that the
     INTERNET says it, so the drawn layer is the figure repeating OUTWARD from
     where it was stated — larger and sparser as it travels. A photograph of a
     screen can show the claim; it cannot show it being repeated.
     Full-frame p-a window, no plate: the echo has to cross the whole picture to
     be an echo, and the p-b edge read as a panel taped over the photo.
motion: tl.fromTo("#s13-echo text", { opacity: 0, scale: 0.82, transformOrigin: "50% 50%" }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out", stagger: 0.13 }, S.s13 + 1.60);

s14.comment:
2.4 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral — IT IS REAL. The National Diet Building

s15.comment:

s16.comment:
2.6 · B · FIGURE · target · THE COLD FLOOR — the coldest ground in the cut,
     because this is where the claim collapses.
     TRUTH: 16px of a 1480px track = 1.08%, which is what 'about 1%' means. The
     previous build drew the identical 16px nub in a 600px track = 2.67% and
     printed 'ABOUT 1%' over it — a drawn proportion 2.4x off a published
     figure. Track width and nub width are a PAIR; never copy one without the
     other. Full-frame p-a, because a 1480px track does not fit an 860px plate.

s17.comment:

     340px against 1.1 as 9.9px, drawn to scale across a full-width band.
     The inline #s17-hi / #s17-lo rects are GONE: the ratio was arithmetically
     right and visually unreadable — two dim rectangles slice-cropped hard right
     inside an 860px plate. A ratio nobody can measure is not a measurement.
     The drawn field that remains is a measuring rule, which is what 'thirty

s19.comment:
2.9 · D · BAND · no role · cool — WHO IS IN. Lottie 3 of 4: 108 households,
     28 of them lit, then everyone. A subset inside a set is the one picture a
     photograph can never state, and the whole debunk turns on it.
     The 28/108 is DELIBERATELY not 37.8% — 37.8% is a share of disposable
     income, not a share of households, and a grid at 37.8% would be a fabricated
     statistic dressed as a real one (see assets/lottie/src/who-is-counted.py).
     Do not 'correct' it.
     Everything turns over on ONE beat at +4.446, the scene's declared framing
     boundary: the photo swaps (motion lives in the shipped cut), the fence
     around the counted minority goes, the brackets open past both edges, and
     the Lottie's second pass lights everyone. The Lottie starts at +1.98 for
     exactly that reason — its phase 2 begins at frame 74 of 135, i.e. 54.8%
     through a 4.50s play = +2.47, and 1.98 + 2.47 = 4.446.

s20.comment:
2.10 · D · BAND · warn · red — ONLY ONE OF THEM TRAVELS. Lottie 4 of 4:
     concentric rings leave one token and not the other. Travel is motion by
     definition and a still page cannot state it; this is the one scene in the
     chapter where the Lottie IS the argument.
     D, not A: the mechanism owns the lower two-thirds, so the type cannot sit
     in the middle of it. `centred: false` is explicit — the default would
     re-centre an art-off D and drop the stack straight onto the Lottie.
     No drawn rings on top of the Lottie: it already radiates. Two radiating
     things is one too many.

s21.comment:
